text:
maria: FYI brought up `orion-13b-int4v2` on staging with 32k context and ran the long-prefill suite. Seeing weird non-monotonic quality drop when prefill length crosses ~8k tokens. suspecting a KV timestamp split during prefill.

alex: can you paste the minimal repro? logs or a curl? :eyes:

maria: quick repro below — run the prefill harness with --longprefill and seed=42. noticed dropout at token ~8192 -> 8201 where next tokens diverge.

jia: dump from the logs: 
```
[2024-10-19T14:12:01Z] prefill.start id=pf-9a3e tokens=9216 model=orion-13b-int4v2
[2024-10-19T14:12:10Z] kvcache.append shard=0 window=8192->12288 timestamp=1700504319
[2024-10-19T14:12:10Z] kvcache.prefill.handshake mismatch_prefill_id pf-9a3e vs pf-9a3e:ok
[2024-10-19T14:12:11Z] decode.token 8191 tok=... prob=0.012
[2024-10-19T14:12:11Z] decode.token 8202 tok=... prob=0.0009  <-- sudden drop
```

jia: also saw a small WARNING: `rope.scale_mismatch` around the same window.

ci-bot: deploy job 8842 finished on staging (orion-13b-int4v2) — approx 10m ago. artifacts: https://ci.internal/reports/8842/longprefill.log

sami: two hypotheses: (1) RoPE rescaling code path gets triggered when kvcache window grows (we rebase rotary offsets), and quantized kernels (int4v2) have slight numeric bins that amplify the drift; (2) timestamp split causes a prefilling handshake to replay a stale KV page leading to prefix misalignment.

elliott: +1 on both. i ran a narrow experiment toggling `enable_rope_rescale` off and the drop disappears in a couple runs. With it on, drop is consistent.

maria: interesting — can you share the exact flags you ran?

elliott: flags: `--enable_rope_rescale=true --kvcache-window=8192` vs `--enable_rope_rescale=false --kvcache-window=12288`. small perf hit with rescale off but more stable.

alex: could this be quant-specific? have we seen same on fp16 or int8?

maria: quick table from my runs: 
- fp16/rescale=true: small jitter, no large drop
- int8/rescale=true: occasional spike, much smaller than int4
- int4v2/rescale=true: consistent non-monotonic drop at window boundary

jia: i can reproduce locally on my devbox with the int4 kernels. attaching minimal script: 
```
# reproduce.sh
python tests/prefill_runner.py --model orion-13b-int4v2 --prefill-length 10000 --seed 42 --log-level debug
```

maria: next steps i propose:
1) elliott to run a spectral diff between tokens 8100-8300 with rescale on/off (to confirm ropecorruption vs quantization amplification)
2) jia to add extra metadata to kvcache handshake logs (prefill_id + page_hash) and re-run the failing jobs
3) ops to run controlled 10-run sweep on staging for fp16,int8,int4v2 (i can trigger)
4) if ropecorruption confirmed, cherry-pick the safe-rescale guard (PR #6578) into staging for further smoke

alex: tagging @ci-bot for a rerun with additional env: `KV_LOG_EXTRA=1` and `ROPE_RESCALE_DEBUG=1` :thinking:

ci-bot: scheduled job 8850: runs=10 matrix=[fp16,int8,int4v2] flags=[KV_LOG_EXTRA=1,ROPE_RESCALE_DEBUG=1]. ETA ~12m.

maria: thanks all — i'll collect the diffs and open a short MR with the failing trace and minimal repro. will add the token-diff csv in the MR.

elliott: if someone hits it locally, try toggling `--kvcache-page-size` smaller (4096) as a stopgap — reduced the failure frequency in one run.

alex: awesome. if we confirm it's an int4 amplification of tiny numeric drift, we should add it to the onboarding checklist for quant models (longprefill smoke at multiple window boundaries).

maria: agreed — i'll draft a checklist item and link to the MR. ping me if you want access to the staging run logs. :thumbsup:
